pr_title: Actually try port when finding next available port for ssdp server
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The function to find a free port for the SSDP server does not actually try the port(s), but actually uses port 0 in which case the OS allocates a port. This usually succeeds, and the function returns the first port within the range of `40000..40100`. As a result, the server tries to bind to port 40000 regardless whether this port is actually free or not.

issue_context.title: Finding free TCP port does not work properly in SSDP component
issue_context.body:
### The problem

The following code is executed to find a free TCP port in [components/ssdp/\_\_init\_\_.py](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/ssdp/__init__.py#L665)


``` 
for port in range(UPNP_SERVER_MIN_PORT, UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT):
        try:
            test_socket.bind(source)
            return port
        except OSError:
            if port == UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT:
                raise

    raise RuntimeError("unreachable")
```

Note how the `port` variable is not used for testing the socket. The MIN_PORT and MAX_PORT are 40000 and 40100, so as far as I can tell either the bind will succeed immediately and port 40000 is returned, or the bind will fail 100 times and SSDP fails to start. This occurs for example with this user: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/ssdp-still-not-up/501467/2
It's also failing for me. So far, I only see reports of this failing on Dockerized Raspberry Pi deployments.
I'm not familiar enough with Linux sockets to propose a fix, so I'm hoping someone can help out.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.12.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

SSDP

comments: Thank you for this issue @JakobStruye, nice find. I've created a PR to fix this.

@StevenLooman Thanks for the fix. Can you also check the following line in the same function: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/8e82ba0d6eb55c0b1dbe1abda842b2d81821ef2c/homeassistant/components/ssdp/__init__.py#L671
This `if port == UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT:` will never be true as port only goes up to `UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT - 1`
I guess it should be `if port == UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT -1:`

Looks like this doesn't fix the issue of the `test_socket.bind` failing in Raspberry Pi Docker containers. I'll investigate further and open another issue if needed.

> Looks like this doesn't fix the issue of the `test_socket.bind` failing in Raspberry Pi Docker containers. I'll investigate further and open another issue if needed.

Thank you for investigating. Feel free to report here as the PR isn't merged yet.

> This if port == UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT: will never be true as port only goes up to UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT - 1
I guess it should be if port == UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT -1:

You are absolutely right. `range()` isn't inclusive regarding the `stop` parameter. Changed!

review_comments: Is this correct, or is the range wrong? Maybe it doesn't matter?

`range()` is exclusive regarding the `stop` value. I.e., `range(UPNP_SERVER_MIN_PORT, UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT)` results in `UPNP_SERVER_MIN_PORT..UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT - 1`.

When the last port is tested, the `port` value is `UPNP_SERVER_MAX_PORT - 1`. If the port is not free, we want to re-raise the `OSError`.
